title: Linearity of the prescribed ordinary root-limit comparison
statement: For a prime l, a scheme X and a strict constant Z_l-module tower H whose underlying additive tower is isomorphic to the prescribed roots-of-unity tower, there is an isomorphism from the restriction of the completed root module to lim H. Its underlying additive map is exactly the inverse of diagonalRootLimitComparison. No invertibility of l on X, derived-category assumption or completeness hypothesis is needed.

source.place: paragraph (1), target ordinary root inverse limit

proof.text: Every section in level n of the root tower is killed by l^(n+1). For an additive map into a module killed by l^r, PadicInt.appr_spec approximates each p-adic scalar by an integer; the difference is divisible by l^r, so the additive map commutes with the scalar action. Apply this to each coordinate of the inverse additive root comparison. The resulting module-linear maps are natural and compatible by faithfulness of scalar forgetting. Form the cone and its unique module-limit lift. Forgetting preserves limits, so the underlying lift is exactly the given inverse by the joint monicity of all projections. Scalar forgetting reflects isomorphisms, hence this lift is invertible.

proof_origin.place: paragraph (1); sectionwise prime-power-torsion linearity and limit universal property

mathlib_searches.query: An additive map between p-adic modules into a module killed by a power of p is automatically p-adic linear
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: adic completion map and lift constructions, PadicInt.mahlerTerm_apply and PadicInt.toZModPow. None upgrades an arbitrary additive map into prime-power torsion to p-adic linearity.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Construct the linear lift directly using finite torsion and the limit universal property.

mathlib_searches.results: One hit: PadicInt.appr_spec in Mathlib.NumberTheory.Padics.RingHoms states that x minus its integer approximation belongs to the prime-power ideal.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Use this ideal divisibility to prove the automatic scalar-linearity lemma.

mathlib_searches.results: The interface already constructs the additive root comparison. No existing theorem lifts that comparison to constant p-adic modules; higher endpoint consumers assume it.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Prove the sectionwise torsion argument and the unique linear limit lift.

lean.statement:
theorem root_limit_iso (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (H : DiagonalSystems l X)
    (roots : H ⋙ diagonalForget l X ≅
      Scheme.proEtaleRootsOfUnityTower X l (Fact.out : l.Prime)) :
    ∃ t : (diagonalCompletedRestriction l X).obj (Scheme.purTwistZlModule X l) ≅ limit H,
      HEq ((diagonalForget l X).map t.hom)
        (diagonalRootLimitComparison l X H roots).inv
